title: Private Deploy Field Notes - Maya Chen
content:
Quick field notes / scratchpad for customer A (on-prem / VPC) -- messy, not final.

2026-02-20: initial kickoff with infra+customer. customer is air-gapped, hitting compliance rules (no outbound internet from control plane).

High-level constraints:
- Must support air-gapped install (no direct pull from Docker Hub).
- Customer uses internal artifact registry at artifactory.corp.example (reachable only from mgmt VLAN).
- KMS is AWS KMS in a VPC endpoint via proxy (need to confirm egress rules).
- Dedicated GPU nodes (NVIDIA A40), Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, containerd runtime.
- Firewall: only ports 22, 443 allowed from mgmt jump host; nodes cannot reach internet.

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm exact artifactory repo path for container images (ASK: ops point-of-contact). Ticket: RDP-5678.
- [ ] Prepare tarball of helm charts + images (airgap bundle). script: tools/make-airgap.sh (WIP)
- [ ] Validate customer GPU driver versions: they reported driver 525.85 but need 510+ for CUDA11.8. Ask SRE for compatibility matrix.
- [ ] Verify KMS access pattern: will we call KMS via proxy or provide encrypted secrets blob? get clarity from security.
- [ ] Prepare step-by-step install runbook (short checklist for on-site eng).

Install notes (rough):
1) Pre-reqs on admin jump host:
   - Ensure jump host has vpn/ssh access to mgmt VLAN.
   - Place airgap bundle under /opt/redwood-airgap/
   - Ensure helm v3.9+ installed, kubectl matching cluster version.

2) Nodes prep (run as root / sudo):
   - apt update && apt install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
   - Install nvidia-driver: verify vendor installer; recommended: 510.x or 525.x -- confirm with runtime team.
   - Install containerd 1.6+ and configure cgroup v2 if required.
   - Set sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=1, disable swap.

3) Airgap image load:
   - On a machine with docker/containerd access: 
     ctr images import /opt/redwood-airgap/images.tar.gz 
     helm install redwood ./charts --values values.prod.yaml --namespace redwood
   - Note: images must be pre-loaded to node containerd; our helm relies on imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

Common blockers seen so far:
- Customer registry uses self-signed certs; need CA bundle to be added to /etc/ssl/certs on nodes and jump host.
- KMS via proxy: control plane needs to be able to reach KMS endpoint through a narrow set of IPs; customer is pushing back on opening extra egress. Might need local HSM or bring-your-own-encryption option.
- GPU driver mismatches causing CUDA failures in runtime: observed segfaults when driver < required by pytorch + torch-cuda combo.
- SELinux enforced on some hosts (unexpected). Need to add SELinux policy or require permissive.

Debugging checklist (for onsite):
- If inference pod OOMs on startup: check node memory pressure, check device plugin logs (/var/log/nvidia-device-plugin.log).
- If container cannot pull images: check containerd config and image store, confirm images loaded locally.
- If KMS errors in logs: full error includes TLS handshake fail vs 403; TLS -> CA bundle issue, 403 -> IAM/network policy.
- If GPU device not visible: nvidia-smi missing -> driver not installed correctly (check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log).

Helpful commands to paste to customer (short):
- systemctl status containerd
- journalctl -u kubelet -f --since "2m"
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
- ctr images ls | grep redwood

Customer env reminders:
- Management VLAN: 10.45.0.0/24 (jump host reachable)
- Compute VLAN: 10.46.0.0/22 (no outbound)
- Artifactory: artifactory.corp.example:443 (only reachable from mgmt)
- KMS proxy: kms-proxy.internal:8443 (proxy endpoint for KMS calls)
- Admin contacts: ops@cust.example, secops@cust.example (cc Riley on escalations)

Open questions/decisions to make:
- Can customer allow egress to a narrow set of Redwood CDN IPs for metrics/reporting? (would avoid full airgap complexity)
- If not, do we provide a local telemetry relay agent they run on mgmt host? How does that affect support/debugging?
- Encryption: local keywrap vs remote KMS. Which is acceptable for them?

Notes from 2026-02-25 call (Riley + Aisha):
- Riley: will produce airgap artifact builder by EOD 2026-02-27 (PR #322). Need manifest version pinning.
- Aisha: will draft runbook; focus on minimal interactive steps for onsite eng.
- Maya: follow up on driver compat with runtime and provide a quick compatibility table (driver -> CUDA -> runtime).

Quick driver-compat sketch (to validate):
- Nvidia driver 510.x -> CUDA 11.6/11.7 -> good for older runtime
- Nvidia driver 525.x -> CUDA 11.8 -> recommended for latest optimized kernels
- Confirm with infra team before recommending upgrades (some customers locked to validated stacks).

Post-install followups:
- Verify metrics pipeline: check prometheus scrape targets (if customer allowed) or confirm local pushgateway config.
- Validate model load times with small internal test (prompt set: 10 short prompts) and log p50/p95 latency.
- Run an end-to-end smoke test: start controller, ensure KV cache warm-up, send 100 requests and capture errors.

Random notes to self:
- Bring extra USB keys with CA bundle & airgap tar (zip) on-site.
- Print minimal runbook: 1-page checklist for onsite eng.
- Ask sales/CS for customer change window (maintenance windows) before rebooting nodes for driver upgrade.

Attachments to produce:
- airgap bundle (images.tar.gz)
- helm chart tarball (charts.tar.gz) pinned versions
- one-page runbook PDF
- compatibility matrix CSV

Status: waiting on artifactory path + driver confirmation. Next sync 2026-03-03 (internal).

-- end scratchpad --
